changes.bio: Cincinnati sprinter Mary Wineberg won an Olympic gold medal with the United States 4x400-meter relay team in Beijing in 2008. A 2002 UC education graduate, she set a Bearcats 400-meter record during her collegiate career and was selected for the UC Athletics Hall of Fame Class of 2010.

changes.bio: Jim Herman played golf for Cincinnati from 1996 to 2000 and was inducted into the UC Athletics Hall of Fame in 2015. His PGA Tour victories include the 2016 Shell Houston Open, the 2019 Barbasol Championship and the 2020 Wyndham Championship.

changes.bio: Recognized as UC's first Athletics Director, assuming the position in 1918 until 1928. Also served as basketball coach (1918-28), amassing a 106-81 record and winning Buckeye Athletic Association titles in 1926 and 1928. Was head football coach 1918-21, compiling a 12-15-2 record in four seasons. Under his leadership, UC's athletics department emerged from a one-person operation to an eight-person full-time staff. Inaugurated the sales of basketball season tickets, putting that sport on a sound financial base. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1977.

updates.reason: Correct unambiguous typographical error.

changes.bio: Persistence--he was cut from his high school team three times--not only landed him a spot on the varsity as a senior but launched a career that took him to college and professional stardom and a place in the National Basketball Hall of Fame. Impressive play on the junior varsity earned him a berth on the varsity midway through his freshman season at UC. Led the team in scoring and rebounding in each of his final three seasons, averaging 24.6 points and 16.5 rebounds as a senior. Concluded his career as UC's all-time leader in scoring (1,598 points) and rebounding (1,242). Earned second team All-American honors in 1955 (NEA, International News Service, Tempo) and was an honorable mention choice by Converse. Taken by the Rochester Royals in the 1955 NBA draft, embarking on an 11-season NBA career. Earned six NBA All-Star selections in 11 seasons and finished second in league scoring with a 31.2-point average in 1959-60. Became the legal guardian of Royals teammate Maurice Stokes following his disabling injury in 1958 and helped raise money for Stokes' care. Charter member of the UC Athletics Hall of Fame. Enshrined in the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1983. His jersey No. 27 was retired by UC in 1993.

updates.reason: Correct duplicate wording and facts contradicted by NBA and Naismith Hall records: 1959-60 scoring runner-up and 1983 enshrinement. Remove stale current-rank claim and inaccurate injury description.

changes.bio: One of UC's track and field all-time greats who garnered a total of five All-American awards. First Bearcat track athlete to qualify for the NCAA Championships in all four seasons, competing in both the long jump and triple jump at the outdoor championships. Earned All-American honors as a junior with a third place finish in the triple jump. Capped his career by capturing All-American plaudits in both the long jump (second place) and triple jump (sixth) as a senior. Also qualified for the NCAA Indoor Championships in the long jump and triple jump his junior and senior campaigns, garnering All-American honors each year in the triple jump. Closed his career holding UC records in both the long jump (26'1 1/2") and triple jump (55'6 1/2"). Narrowly missed earning a berth on the U.S. Olympic Team at the 1972 Trials. Competed on the U.S. Army team that made a tour of China in 1975. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1988.

updates.reason: Correct unambiguous copy errors; preserve unreviewed statistics.

changes.bio: Originally joined the track and field team as a walk-on during his sophomore season and quickly blossomed into one of the team's top point-scorers, specializing in the 400 and 800 meter events. Team captain his junior and senior seasons. Capped his career with an eighth place finish in the 800 at the 1987 NCAA Outdoor Championships, posting a school-record time of 1:47.00. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1999.

changes.bio: Long before he attained the title "Mr. Versatility" as a professional, he demonstrated his variety of skills as a Bearcat. Began his career as a quarterback, leading the team in passing as a freshman. Moved to halfback as a sophomore and was the team's top ground-gainer his junior campaign. Also led UC in receiving in 1958 and was the team scoring leader his freshman and junior seasons. Rugged member of the secondary who led UC in interceptions in three of his four seasons. Returned a pair of interceptions for touchdowns as a freshman, scoring from 87 and 88 yards. Held UC career interception return yardage record when he graduated, a mark since tied. Closed his career as UC's all-time leading scorer (127 points). Earned All-Missouri Valley Conference honors as a sophomore. Played in the North-South, Senior Bowl and College All-Star games. Selected in the third round of the 1959 NFL Draft by the New York Giants and continued to display his versatility during his 13 seasons with the club, setting team records as a receiver. Successful head coach on the major college level. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1978.

changes.bio: Outstanding football player who continued his love of the Bearcats through lifetime support of the program. Three-year letterwinner as a rugged lineman. Team captain as a senior. Inducted into the Sigma Sigma honorary. One of the founders of UNOCIN, an early organization that raised financial support for football. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1980.

changes.bio: Sid Gillman was the architect of what is considered the greatest era of UC football. His teams compiled a 50-13-1 record in six seasons, won three Mid-American Conference championships and played in a pair of bowl games. Originator of the passing game now considered the West Coast Offense, Gillman began developing that attack while at UC, earning national aerial game rankings. Left UC to become head coach of the Los Angeles Rams and launch a pro coaching career. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1981.

additions.name: Mike Kinnett
